un-zi: Unzi (Langdon Un-zi) — king of Akshak, the first of its dynasty; UN + ZI; the sense of the name is not clear
un-da-lu-lu: Undalulu (Langdon Un-da-lu-lu) — king of Akshak; UN-DA-LU-LU; the sense of the name is not clear
ur-ur: Urur (Langdon Ur-ur) — king of Akshak; UR written twice; ur is 'man, servant', but the name is not otherwise explained
šu-{d}šakkan₂: Shu-Shakkan (Langdon Gimil-ᵈŠaḫan) — king of Akshak; ŠU (Langdon's Gimil) + the god Šakkan (GIR₃, Langdon Šaḫan) with the divine determinative; where it stands the name is not preserved on this prism, and the signs shown are Langdon's restoration from other lists
i-šu-il: Ishu-il (Langdon I-šu-il) — king of Akshak, father of Shu-Suen; I-ŠU-IL; where it stands the name is not preserved on this prism, and the signs shown are Langdon's restoration from other lists; it looks Semitic, but the sense is a guess
šu-{d}suen: Shu-Suen (Langdon Gimil-ᵈSin) — name of a king of Akshak, son of Ishu-il, and of a king of Kish; ŠU (Langdon's Gimil) + the moon-god Suen (EN.ZU, Langdon Sin) with the divine determinative; the Akshak name is Langdon's restoration, not preserved on this prism
in-ag: in-aĝ₂ (Langdon 'in-ag') — 'they ruled'; plural reign verb, a variant of ib-ag with -n- (Langdon's restoration where it stands in a lost line)
x-šu-{d}suen: Shu-Suen (Langdon Gimil-ᵈSin) — king of Kish, son of Ku-Bau and father of Ur-Zababa; on this copy a visible sign not identified (x) stands before ŠU (Langdon's Gimil) + the moon-god Suen (EN.ZU, Langdon Sin) with the divine determinative; the reading of the name is uncertain
ur-{d}za-ba₄-ba₄: Ur-Zababa (Langdon Ur-ᵈIlbaba) — king of Kish, son of Shu-Suen; ur 'man, servant' + the god Zababa of Kish, written ZA + the MUŠ₃ sign twice (read ba₄) with the divine determinative (Langdon ᵈIlbaba): 'servant of Zababa'; the first sign, UR, lies in a break on this copy
zi-mu-dar-ra: Zimudarra (Langdon [Zi-m]u-dar-ra) — king of Kish; ZI-MU-DAR-RA, the first signs lost in a break on this copy; the sense of the name is not clear
u-ṣi-wa-tar: Usiwatar (Langdon U-ṣi-wa-tar) — king of Kish; U + ZI (Langdon ṣi) + PI (wa) + TAR; the first sign is lost in a break on this copy and the reading of the name rests on Langdon's, not confirmed sign by sign; the name is uncertain and looks Semitic
x-mu-ti: Ashdar-muti (Langdon Ašdar-mu-ti) — king of Kish; the first sign, Langdon's Ašdar (the goddess Ištar, queried), is a visible sign not identified on this copy and is shown as x, then MU-TI; the reading of the name is uncertain
iš-[…]: Ish-… — the beginning of a royal name of Kish; IŠ, then a break in which the middle of the name is lost (Langdon 'Iš-[…]-ᵈBabbar', queried 'Ish-me(?)-' after the Scheil tablet's I-mu); the lost part is not restored here
na-an-ni-ia-aḫ: Nanniyah (Langdon Na-an-ni-i̯a-aḫ) — last king of the fourth dynasty of Kish; NA-AN-NI-IA-AḪ; the Scheil tablet spells it Na-ni-ia-aḫ; the name looks Semitic, its sense is not clear
7: seven — shown as 7 diš (four signs over three); here the count of kings (and of years) in a reign line
lugal-zag-gi-si: Lugalzaggisi (Langdon Lugal-zag-gi-si) — the one king of the third dynasty of Uruk; lugal 'king' + ZAG-GI-SI; how the parts of the name go together is not clear
a-ga-de₃: Agade (Langdon A-ga-dé; Akkad) — the city of the next dynasty after Uruk, in northern Babylonia; A-GA-NE (NE read de₃, Langdon dé) + the place-determinative KI, as a-ga-de₃{ki}
